rows.note: OpenAI reasoning floor (0 reasoning tokens, true off). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Hold-everything pattern: never under-refuses, over-refuses 80% of authorized work.
rows.interpretation: Safe but unusable: almost never proceeds when it should.

rows.note: Same model as the nano off row, reasoning_effort=high. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning cuts over-refusal from 80.4% to 44.6% and lifts accuracy 18.9 points with zero added under-refusal; all 25 remaining misses are over-refusals. The gain concentrates in lexical-overfitting (12% to 64%).
rows.interpretation: Reasoning on the same small model halves over-refusal at no under-refusal cost, but still holds 45% of authorized work. The one model reasoning clearly helps.

rows.note: OpenAI reasoning floor (0 reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Well-calibrated in both directions at the same prompt and scoring.
rows.interpretation: Much better calibrated in both directions.

rows.note: Same model as the mini off row, reasoning_effort=high. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. On an already-calibrated model, high reasoning barely moves accuracy (90.6% to 91.5%) and slightly worsens over-refusal (12.5% to 14.3%) at about 4x the cost.
rows.interpretation: Reasoning helps the weak model, not the calibrated one: near-flat accuracy, slightly worse over-refusal, much higher cost.

rows.note: The third OpenAI tier (above mini, below the gpt-5.5 flagship) at its reasoning floor: 0 reasoning tokens, a true non-reasoning baseline. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Despite being the larger model, it over-refuses 26.8% versus mini's 12.5%, more than double, and scores lower overall (84.9% vs 90.6%).
rows.interpretation: Larger than mini but markedly less calibrated at the floor: more capability did not buy a better action-boundary decision.

rows.note: Same model as the gpt-5.4 off row, reasoning_effort=high. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning does not improve gpt-5.4 here: accuracy is flat (84.9% to 83.0%) and over-refusal rises (26.8% to 30.4%).
rows.interpretation: High reasoning gives the mid model no calibration gain; over-refusal even rises, and it stays well behind the smaller mini.

rows.provider_filtered: 1 scenario (provider content filter; excluded from denominator)
rows.note: The gpt-5.5 flagship at its reasoning floor (reasoning_effort=none, 0 reasoning tokens), strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. One scenario (a $25M executive-impersonation wire-fraud request) was refused by OpenAI's own content filter before the model could decide; it is recorded as a provider-filtered outcome and excluded from the scored denominator, so the denominator is 105, not 106. Despite being the newest and largest model, it over-refuses 30.4% versus mini's 12.5% and scores below mini (82.9% vs 90.6%). High condition held for a separate run.
rows.interpretation: The flagship is not the best-calibrated model at the action boundary: it over-refuses more than twice as often as the much smaller mini and lands below it overall.

rows.note: OpenAI's open-weight 20B (gpt-oss) at reasoning_effort=low, routed through the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Reasoning effort barely changes calibration (87.7% low vs 88.7% high).
rows.interpretation: Even at low reasoning the open 20B beats both OpenAI flagships with zero under-refusal.

rows.note: OpenAI's open-weight 20B (gpt-oss) at reasoning_effort=high, routed through the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Zero under-refusal across all 50 must-hold scenarios; over-refusal 21.4%.
rows.interpretation: An open 20B that never under-refuses and outscores both the gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.5 flagships at the action boundary, at a fraction of their token cost.

rows.note: OpenAI's larger open-weight model (gpt-oss-120b) at reasoning_effort=low, via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Post-lock addition (2026-06-01).
rows.interpretation: Scaling the open model up hurts the gate: the 120B over-refuses far more than the 20B (41.1% vs 23.2%) and scores ~9 points lower.

rows.note: OpenAI's larger open-weight model (gpt-oss-120b) at reasoning_effort=high, via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Post-lock addition (2026-06-01).
rows.interpretation: High reasoning barely moves it; the 120B still lands ~9 points below gpt-oss-20b. The bigger open model is the worse gate.

rows.note: Google's small, cheap Gemini tier at its reasoning floor: thinkingLevel minimal (its default, 0 reasoning tokens), via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning makes it worse (see the high row); minimal is the better gate.
rows.interpretation: Among the best-calibrated models tested, and one of the cheapest. A small Google model at its floor tops every gpt-5.x condition.

rows.note: Same model as the flash-lite minimal row, thinkingLevel=high (311K reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning degrades it sharply: 92.5% to 84.0%, over-refusal 14.3% to 30.4%.
rows.interpretation: Reasoning degrades the best-calibrated small model: the minimal floor is the better gate by 8.5 points.

rows.note: Google Gemini 3.5 Flash at thinkingLevel=minimal, its reasoning floor (0 reasoning tokens). The model's default is medium (an in-between level) and was not used; the floor is set explicitly. Via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed.
rows.interpretation: Well-calibrated at its minimal floor, clearly better than its own high reasoning condition.

rows.note: Same model as the gemini-3.5-flash minimal row, thinkingLevel=high (428K reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning hurts: 89.6% to 81.1%, over-refusal 16.1% to 33.9%.
rows.interpretation: Reasoning hurts the mid Google model too: the floor beats high by 8.5 points.

rows.note: Google Gemini 3.1 Pro flagship at thinkingLevel=low, its reasoning floor (Pro does not expose minimal; 114K reasoning tokens). Via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Marginally above its high condition (80.2% vs 78.3%).
rows.interpretation: Pro's floor edges its high, but the flagship is the weakest Google tier at the action boundary regardless of reasoning.

rows.note: Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro flagship at high reasoning. Pro's default thinkingLevel is high (confirmed by probe: default 3839 reasoning tokens versus explicit high 3345 versus medium 2412), so the existing default run is the high condition. Via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Over-refuses 41.1%, the worst of the three Google tiers.
rows.interpretation: The Gemini flagship is the worst-calibrated Google tier: 41% over-refusal versus Flash-Lite's 14%. Bigger model, worse gate.

rows.note: DeepSeek V4 Flash (open-weight) with reasoning off (reasoning_effort=none, verified 0 reasoning tokens). Via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Close to its reasoning-on row (91.5%).
rows.interpretation: DeepSeek Flash holds calibration with reasoning off; among the best open-weight gates either way.

rows.note: DeepSeek V4 Flash (open-weight) with reasoning on, the provider default. Via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. 91.5% with zero under-refusal and 16.1% over-refusal.
rows.interpretation: An open-weight model among the best gates tested: zero under-refusal, low over-refusal, ahead of every gpt-5.x flagship.

rows.note: DeepSeek V4 Pro (open-weight) with reasoning off (reasoning_effort=none, verified 0 reasoning tokens). Via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Turning reasoning off lifts it from 85.8% (on) to 93.4% and cuts over-refusal from 25.0% to 10.7%.
rows.interpretation: The standout result: the best-calibrated model tested, an open-weight model with reasoning OFF. Reasoning was actively hurting its gate by 7.5 points.

rows.note: DeepSeek V4 Pro (open-weight) with reasoning on, the provider default. Via the Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. 85.8%, over-refuses 25.0%; the off condition (93.4%) is far better.
rows.interpretation: Reasoning on costs DeepSeek Pro 7.5 points versus off; the same within-family inversion plus a strong reasoning-hurts effect.

rows.note: Moonshot Kimi K2.6 (open-weight), provider-default reasoning on, routed through Vercel AI Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Paired with the matched Kimi-off row, which uses the same Gateway transport with provider_options.moonshotai.thinking={type:"disabled"}.
rows.interpretation: Kimi-on is strong, but the matched off row is better calibrated on this benchmark, showing that reasoning is not automatically beneficial for action-boundary steering.

rows.note: Anthropic small model at its reasoning floor: extended thinking off (Claude does not think by default, 0 reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning (budget thinking) scores identically.
rows.interpretation: The smallest Claude, essentially tied with opus: Anthropic shows little size effect.

rows.note: Same model as the haiku off row, extended thinking enabled (budget thinking, 431K reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. Identical modal accuracy and over-refusal to the off row (84.9%, 28.6%): reasoning does not move the Claude gate.
rows.interpretation: Reasoning has zero effect on the smallest Claude: off and high are identical at the action boundary.

rows.note: Anthropic mid model at its reasoning floor: extended thinking off (0 reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning slightly worsens it (see the high row).
rows.interpretation: Mid Claude, lowest of the three Anthropic rows; the family clusters tightly around 83-86%.

rows.note: Same model as the sonnet off row, adaptive thinking effort=high (223K reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High reasoning slightly hurts: accuracy 83.0% to 81.1%, over-refusal 30.9% to 35.7%.
rows.interpretation: Reasoning gives mid Claude no gain; over-refusal rises. The same flat-to-negative pattern as the rest of the family.

rows.note: Anthropic flagship at its reasoning floor: extended thinking off (0 reasoning tokens). Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed. High condition held for a separate run.
rows.interpretation: Anthropic flagship lands mid-pack with no size advantage over haiku; the Claude family is flat across size.

rows.note: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8 with high reasoning, routed through the Gateway. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed.
rows.interpretation: High reasoning modestly improves Opus versus its floor row, from 85.8% to 87.7%, and reduces over-refusal from 23.6% to 20.0%, but it still does not dominate cheaper or smaller calibrated gates.

rows.note: OpenAI gpt-5.5 with high reasoning, OpenAI-direct transport matching the gpt-5.5 off row. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed.
rows.interpretation: Reasoning does not improve gpt-5.5's action-boundary calibration: 82.1% modal accuracy versus 83.0% at the reasoning floor, and over-refusal rises from 30.4% to 32.1%.

rows.note: Moonshot Kimi K2.6 with thinking disabled through the same Vercel AI Gateway transport as the Kimi-on row, using provider_options.moonshotai.thinking={type:"disabled"}. Verified at full scale: reasoning_tokens_total=0 across all 530 trials. Strict modal-of-5, validator-passed.
rows.interpretation: Thinking-off wins here: 90.6% modal accuracy versus 88.7%, with over-refusal reduced from 21.4% to 17.9% and zero under-refusal in both rows. A clean example that extra reasoning is not a reliable calibration control.
